thread:
Ajay: Heads-up — CI caught a perf regression on the INT8 path this morning for `gpt-medium` workloads. Per-token p50 jumped ~18% on tail-heavy prompts. Anyone seen this in prod traces?
Maria: saw alerts around 05:12 UTC, linked to increased tail latency on /v1/generate. Not a full outage but SLO drift. :eyes:
Kei: I ran a quick flamegraph on the failing job. Kernel selection flipped from `gemm_fp8_v3` to `gemm_int8_v2_fallback` on many sequences after calibration step. Suspect calibration stats are nudging the selector into the slower kernel for long sequences.
Ajay: can you paste the profiler output?
Kei: sure — trimmed output from the run:
```
summary: per_token_ms: 0.74
  kernel_exec: 0.42
  kv_lookup: 0.10
  kv_cache_miss_penalty: 0.85
  memcpy_host_to_device: 0.03
  kernel_switch_overhead: 0.08
kernel_counters:
  gemm_fp8_v3: 120k
  gemm_int8_v2_fallback: 85k
  gemm_int4_experimental: 4k
  small_matmul_fastpath: 30k
```
Kei: interestingly, kv_cache_hit_rate dropped from 92% to 78% on the same traffic window. Cache miss penalty is punching through on long contexts.
Eva: any recent change to batching heuristics? We adjusted batch sizing for low-latency steady-state last week. Could that raise cache churn?
Sam: the autosizer change reduced max_batch_wait_ms from 8 -> 4ms in the canary, so smaller batches. That could increase per-request context switching and evict KV entries sooner.
Ajay: timeline: autosizer tweak (Apr 2), INT8 calibration tweak (Apr 3), alerts (Apr 4). Seems correlated.
Maria: iops and device memory pressure look higher during regression window. I posted the trace link: https://console.internal/r/trace/0x9a7 — includes token-level spans.
Ajay: looking at token-level spans, kernel_switch_overhead spikes when kernel selection toggles mid-request (e.g., FP8 -> INT8 path). That adds ~0.08-0.15ms per switch, but compounded over long sequences.
Kei: calibration changed quant scale heuristic: now uses per-layer running variance with smaller warmup. For borderline layers that used FP8 before, it's falling back to INT8 which has different kernel codegen and slower matmul kernels for long sequences.
Eva: so two contributors: higher cache miss rate (evictions) + more kernel switches due to calibration borderline decisions + smaller batches. All additive.
Sam: action items: (1) roll-back max_batch_wait_ms in the canary to 8ms, (2) pin calibration config for the INT8 rollout and re-run perf tests, (3) add kernel-selection drift alert with counter beacons.
Ajay: agree. Also want an observability metric: per-token breakdown exported to the console as three counters per model-version: kernel_exec_ms, kv_lookup_ms, kernel_switch_count. Then we can alert if kernel_switch_count per 1k tokens > threshold.
Maria: I can add the dashboards. For now I'll throttle the canary to avoid customer exposure.
Kei: I'll run a microbenchmark: fixed-seed long-context workload and sweep calibration params (warmup window, per-layer vs global scale). Will post results in ~2h.
Eva: can we record a short regression postmortem after fixes? Put the perf deltas and steps we took.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline report — rollback initiated for canary group cg-17 by Maria at 2026-04-04T06:45:12Z.
Ajay: Thanks. Also, we should add a per-kernel performance regression test to CI that runs the long-seq KV-heavy workload to catch this earlier.
Sam: noted for the runtime perf suite. I’ll add the test and a gating alert.
Kei: initial microbench results (sanity):
```
config A (calib warmup=2000): per_token_ms=0.68, kernel_switch_count=12/1000 tokens, kv_hit=91%
config B (calib warmup=500): per_token_ms=0.78, kernel_switch_count=46/1000 tokens, kv_hit=79%
config C (forced fp8 prefer): per_token_ms=0.66, kernel_switch_count=4/1000 tokens, kv_hit=90%
```
Kei: seems warmup reduction causes more fallback to INT8. For now forcing fp8-prefer fixes perf but we need to evaluate quality impact.
Ajay: prioritize perf for production SLO, but schedule quality evals against held-out prompts. If quality regression is small, prefer fp8 prefer by default for these model families.
Maria: rolling canary back now is reducing latency on cg-17. Will monitor for 30m then promote if stable.
Eva: thanks team. Please document the calibration knobs and TL;DR in the ops runbook.
Ajay: will do. Closing thread after we confirm the postmortem and the CI test. :thumbsup:
